Title: The Echoes of Jahiliyyah: A Warning Against Mistreating Daughters
Full Content:
Question:

May Allah reward you with goodness. The female questioner, who symbolized her name with H. M., wrote this question in her own words. She mentions that she is a young woman suffering from her father’s harsh treatment, his injustice, oppression, and tyranny—to the extent that she says she sometimes doubts his actual paternity based on what she sees from him and the hurtful things she hears him say.

She says: I will not hide from you that I hate him very much, but at the same time, I pray for his guidance. I frequently fall into insulting him and talking about him behind his back, and I catch myself doing this by seeking forgiveness for him and praying for him. I do not like to confront him, rather I evade him, and he likewise does not ask about me or care about my affairs. However, I try as much as possible to obey him if he commands me. I have tried repeatedly to advise him, but I have not found the full courage to do so, and he also does not give anyone the courage to confront him, nor does he respond to his family or others. Instead, he does whatever his bad companions dictate to him without thinking whether what he is doing is right or wrong, and without considering the consequences of matters. I inform you that he is well-educated, and he frequently repeats certain Hadiths, yet strangely enough, those Hadiths contradict his actions.

My question, Your Eminence Sheikh Muhammad: Is there any sin upon me for not speaking to him and for evading him, given that this happens despite my will? Guide me in light of this, and is this considered Uquq (undutifulness/disobedience to parents)?

Answer:

It is well-known that parents have rights and children have rights; parents have a right over their sons and daughters, and children have a right over their fathers and mothers. However, the right of parents is greater—the right of parents over children is greater than the right of children over parents.

Therefore, I advise you first to be patient with the harm, oppression, and injustice you experience from your father, and I hope that you will receive a great reward from Allah the Almighty for this patience and good treatment. Do not sever ties with him if this behavior occurs from him; rather, reach out to him and draw closer to him, and you will be the winner.

As for the father, I advise him to be a helper to his children—both sons and daughters—in enabling them to honor him, to be gentle with them, and to treat them kindly. He should know that tyranny, inequity, and injustice toward daughters are acts of the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period of ignorance). Indeed, the people of Jahiliyyah were the ones who disliked female children and resented their existence, to the extent that when one of them was given the glad tidings of a girl, his face would darken, and he would suppress his grief (cf. Qur’an, Surah An-Nahl 16:58). He would hide from the people because of the bad news he was given, debating whether he should keep her in humiliation or bury her in the dust. Verily, evil is what they judge.

In Jahiliyyah, out of their aversion to females, when a baby girl was born to a person, he would go and dig a grave for her and bury her alive, na’udhubillah (we seek refuge in Allah). It is even mentioned that some of them would let the daughter grow until she reached the age of discernment or near it, then take her out to the wilderness and dig a hole for her. As some dust got onto his beard, she would gently brush it away to clean it of dirt while he was digging the hole to bury her—na’udhubillah—and then he would bury her. Some of them would have their daughters crying out for help, pleading with them as they were thrown into the pit: “O father! O father!”—yet he would show no mercy, but trample her down instead, na’udhubillah. These hearts are harder than the hearts of wolves. Therefore, anyone who dislikes women and treats them badly bears a resemblance to the people of Jahiliyyah.

My advice to this father is to fear Allah the Almighty regarding the female children He has blessed him with, and to know that if he is patient with them and disciplines them properly, they will be a shield for him against the Fire. Regarding what has come down in the Fiqh of the Sunnah from the Prophet, peace and be upon him, let him be gentle with them so that Allah may be gentle with him when he meets Him on the Day of Resurrection.

Title: Ruling on a Muslim Woman Visiting Her Non-Muslim Family
Full Content:
Question:

Also, among the listener’s questions, she asks: Is a Muslim woman’s visit to her disbelievers’ family considered allegiance to those who oppose Allah and His Messenger? And is the father considered a stranger (non-Mahram) before whom she must not uncover/reveal her adornments?

Answer:

Maintaining ties of kinship is not considered allegiance. Rather, allegiance is one thing, and maintaining ties of kinship is something else entirely. For this reason, Allah the Almighty combined the command to maintain ties with the prohibition of taking [disbelievers] as allies in the same Surah. He stated in Surah Al-Mumtahanah:

“O you who believe! Take not My enemies and your enemies (i.e. disbelievers and polytheists, etc.) as friends, showing affection towards them,…” (Al-Mumtahanah: 1)

“O you who believe! Take not My enemies and your enemies (i.e. disbelievers and polytheists, etc.) as friends, showing affection towards them,…”

And He stated in the same Surah:

“Allah does not forbid you to deal justly and kindly with those who fought not against you on account of religion and did not drive you out of your homes.” (Al-Mumtahanah: 8)

“Allah does not forbid you to deal justly and kindly with those who fought not against you on account of religion and did not drive you out of your homes.”

Thus, keeping ties of kinship is a matter distinct from allegiance. Accordingly, a person must maintain ties with their relatives, even if they are disbelievers, but without showing allegiance, support, or backing for the state of disbelief they are upon.

Likewise, it is permissible to invite them to one’s home, for example; however, alongside that, one should be keen to present Islam to them, advise them, and guide them, so that perhaps Allah may guide them through him.

Question:

Title: Forcing a Son to Marry: Ruling on Parental Pressure and Marriage Choice
Full Content:
Question:

A listener from Jazan says that he wishes to marry a woman he has chosen for himself, but his father disagrees and wants him to marry a relative of theirs, knowing that she does not pray. What should I do? Guide me and advise me, and may you be rewarded.

Answer:

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds, and peace and blessings be upon our Prophet Muhammad, his family, his companions, and those who follow them in righteousness until the Day of Judgment.

Our answer and guidance to the questioner is first to state: It is not permissible for a father to prevent his son from marrying a woman he is pleased with for himself, nor to force him to marry a woman he does not want simply because she is a relative of the father. This is because these matters pertain to a person’s private life, which is a matter of personal choice where one controls his own affairs. Therefore, it is not permissible to force him into something he does not want, nor to prevent him from what he desires. This is regarding the father of the questioner, and I direct advice to him to let his son marry whoever he wishes.

As for the son: He is not obligated to obey his father in this situation—meaning, he is not obligated to obey his father by marrying a woman he does not want and leaving the woman he desires. He has the right to marry the woman he wants, even if his father dislikes it, provided that this woman does not have a flaw in her religion or character.

Especially since the questioner mentions that the woman his father wants him to marry does not pray: A woman who does not pray is not permissible for any Muslim man to marry until she returns to Islam, because whoever leaves the prayer is a disbeliever with a disbelief that expels them from the fold of Islam. Just as it is not permissible to give a woman in marriage to a man who does not pray, it is likewise not permissible for a person to marry a woman who does not pray.

It is not permissible for a father to force his son to marry a woman he does not want, nor to prevent him from marrying a woman he desires if she possesses good character and religion. The son is not obligated to obey his father in this matter, and he has the right to marry whomever he desires. This is not considered Uquq (undutifulness) toward his father.

Title: Is it Permissible to Call a Dead Person 'Al-Marhoom'?
Full Content:
Question:

The questioner has another question, Your Eminence the Sheikh: Is it permissible to use the word “Al-Marhoom” for the dead—for example, to say: “Al-Marhoom so-and-so”? Please advise us and may you be rewarded.

Answer:

If someone says, while speaking about a dead person: “Al-Marhoom” (the deceased or the one who has been shown mercy.) or “Al-Mghfoor lahu” (the forgiven), or something similar, and uses it as a statement of fact (as a report), then that is not permissible. This is because he does not know whether mercy has been attained for the person or not, and a matter of the unknown is not permissible for a person to assert with certainty. Furthermore, this constitutes testifying to his mercy or forgiveness without knowledge, and testifying without knowledge is forbidden.

However, if one says that by way of supplication (du’a) and hope that Allah Almighty will forgive him and have mercy upon him, then there is nothing wrong with it, and no harm in it. There is no difference between saying “Al-Marhoom” or “So-and-so—may Allah have mercy on him,” because both expressions are suitable for use as a report or as a supplication; it depends on the intention of the speaker.

There is no doubt that those who say “So-and-so is marhoom” or “So-and-so is maghfoor lahu” do not intend by this to state a fact and testify that the person has definitely received mercy and forgiveness. Rather, they intend by it hope, optimism, and supplication. Therefore, there is no harm or blame in using this word.

Title: Ruling on Claiming Disbelievers Are Better Than Muslims
Full Content:
Question:

This was already pointed out in the previous lecture by Sheikh Salih Al-Fawzan, during the lecture on the past Friday night, warning against this matter.

The statement made by some people that “the disbeliever is better than the Muslim” or that “Christians are better than Muslims” is apostasy from Islam—we seek refuge in Allah. This is a tremendous evil. Whoever says that the disbelievers are better than the Muslims has imitated the Jews in their statement to the disbelievers: “You are better guided than the believers.” This is a major munkar (reprehensible evil).

Even if a disbeliever strives to improve his goods, market them well, and be truthful in certain business matters, he possesses deep disbelief, misguidance, and immense corruption that indicates his vileness, harmfulness, and corruption, making him among the filthiest and most evil of creatures.

A Muslim, even if he has some sins, is much better than a disbeliever, because he possesses faith in Allah and His Messenger, and he possesses the Tawhid (Oneness) of Allah. He is better than the disbeliever in many respects, even if he has committed some sins violating his religion. Islam forbids him from sins, treachery, and lying. However, this does not mean disbelievers are better than him! Rather, he is better and better-guided than the disbelievers, despite whatever sins he may have. Nevertheless, it is obligatory for him to fear Allah and beware of sins, lying, and treachery.

If a disbeliever strives to be truthful, improve his goods, or perfect his craft for his immediate, worldly benefit, you—O Muslim—must not be lax in this so as not to become a blemish on the Muslims. Rather, you too must strive to master your craft with honesty, without treachery, and with truthfulness, avoiding lies, so that you do not open a door of evil against the Muslims. You must be extremely cautious of everything Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden. However, no Muslim is permitted because of this to say that disbelievers are better than Muslims, or better-guided, or more truthful. This is all falsehood and a tremendous evil, and whoever says this unconditionally has committed “kufr” (disbelief)—we ask Allah for safety.

This is a great affliction, we seek refuge in Allah! Furthermore, it is not permissible to import disbelievers into this Peninsula [Arabian Peninsula], nor is it permissible to employ them for domestic service—whether men or women—or for labor. This Peninsula must be purified of disbelievers; disbelievers must be kept away from it, and none should be imported or employed for it except Muslims, while also thoroughly vetting and exercising caution with Muslims so that only a good Muslim man or woman is employed when the need arises.

As for employing Jews, Christians, Buddhists, or other disbelievers, all of this is a munkar that is not permissible in this Peninsula. The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded the expulsion of the polytheists from this Peninsula, and said: “If I live, I will surely expel the Jews and Christians from it until I leave nothing but a Muslim.” He then reiterated this instruction at the time of his death, peace and blessings be upon him, and Umar subsequently expelled them.

“If I live, I will surely expel the Jews and Christians from it until I leave nothing but a Muslim.”

The point is that this Peninsula is the sanctuary of Islam and its cradle. No second religion is permitted to be established in it; it is never permissible for two religions to remain in it, but rather only a single religion. It is not permissible to bring disbelievers into it except in cases of necessity through the authorities for something that benefits the Muslims and is a necessity—such as an engineer who is needed, or a doctor who is needed, in small, rare quantities upon necessity, just as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, allowed the Jews to stay in Khaybar out of necessity, and then Umar expelled them after the Prophet’s instruction to expel them, peace and blessings be upon him.

The point is that this is a very serious matter that must be guarded against.

Title: Refuting Those Who Say That the Hijab Is Not the Covering of the Face
Full Content:
Question:

I have heard some Saudi Sheikhs saying that women’s hijab is not the covering of the face, but rather the covering of the head, chest, and hands. Do they have evidence for this or not? We kindly ask your Eminence to clarify this matter.

Answer:

As for covering the head and the body, this is a matter upon which there is no disagreement; it is obligatory for her to cover them from all non-mahram men (ajnabis), and this is a known matter. The disagreement among the scholars is specifically regarding the face and hands: must she cover them from a non-mahram—such as her husband’s brother, her sister’s husband, her neighbors, and her paternal cousins—or not?

The legal proofs indicate that the obligation is to cover them, and that adornment is present in them. Indeed, the face is the greatest form of adornment; it is a woman’s index of beauty or plainness, serving as her primary identifier and adornment. Therefore, just as it is obligatory to cover the head, it is also obligatory to cover the face, because the face holds immense significance. Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, said: “And when you ask (his wives) for anything you want, ask them from behind a screen, that is purer for your hearts and for their hearts.” [Al-Ahzab: 53], and He did not make an exception for the face. “People in the pre-Islamic period of ignorance” (Jahiliyyah) and at the very beginning of Islam used to uncover the face, and a woman’s face would be visible, and she would sit with people. Then Allah revealed the hijab, so women were forbidden from uncovering their faces.

“And when you ask (his wives) for anything you want, ask them from behind a screen, that is purer for your hearts and for their hearts.”

This was explained by Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, as reported in the Sahihayn (Al-Bukhari and Muslim) from the Hadith of Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that on the Day of Al-Ifk (the Slander), when she heard the voice of Safwan ibn al-Mu’attal reciting istirja’ (“Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji’un”), she said: “So I covered my face with my veil, and he had seen me before the hijab.” This indicates that after the hijab, faces were no longer seen; seeing [them uncovered] only occurred before the hijab, whereas after the hijab, women would cover their faces with their veils.

“So I covered my face with my veil, and he had seen me before the hijab.”

Similarly, during the Farewell Pilgrimage, she said: “When men approached us, one of us would draw down her outer garment (jilbab) from her head over her face, and when the men moved away, we would uncover [our faces].” All of this indicates that after Allah revealed the verse of hijab, the hijab became general and applied to the head, face, and the rest of the body. This is the preferred view: the obligation of a woman covering her entire body—the face, hands, feet, and the like—because it is an awrah (part of the body that must be covered) and a source of temptation.

Therefore, a believer should take precautions for himself and not indulge in concessions  that lack evidence. A believer should also instill this in his family, teach them, and guide them—his sister, aunt, maternal aunt, wife, and others. Likewise, a woman should fear Allah, guard against the causes of temptation, and not lean toward concessions that have no evidence. We ask Allah to guide us all.

Title: Is Kissing the Black Stone a Form of Paganism?
Full Content:
Question:

Orientalists claim that Islam retained a vestige of paganism, such as kissing the Black Stone. How do you respond to them?

Answer:

This is not paganism; this is something prescribed for us by Allah for a profound wisdom, and in this, we are neither imitating the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic period of ignorance) nor worshipping through Jahiliyyah forms of worship. Allah directs His commands to His servants as He wills, the Glorified and Exalted. When He commands them to do something, it becomes an independent legislation that has no connection to the Jahiliyyah.

Indeed, there were good matters from the Jahiliyyah that Islam approved of: the blood-money (diyah) of one hundred camels was a matter of the Jahiliyyah and Islam approved it; the qasamah (oath of accusation) was from the Jahiliyyah and Islam approved it; and similarly, kissing and touching the Black Stone. This involves the glorification of Allah and seeking His pleasure—it is not seeking blessings from the stone itself or making requests of the stone. Rather, it is obedience to Allah in touching the Black Stone and the Yemeni Corner.

Allah tested His servants through this to see whether they would obey or disobey. When Allah commands them to do something, they comply. Allah instituted the touching of the Black Stone and the Yemeni Corner among them as a trial and a test: would they hear and obey? Would they comply with what Allah has legislated for them or not?

This is why when Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, kissed the Black Stone, he said: “I know that you are a stone that neither harms nor benefits, and had I not seen the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, kissing you, I would not have kissed you.”

“I know that you are a stone that neither harms nor benefits, and had I not seen the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, kissing you, I would not have kissed you.”

Likewise, among the customs of the Jahiliyyah was honoring the guest, and honoring the guest remained in Islam. All of this, along with other noble moral traits that Allah loves and His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, urged [us] to follow—as well as all good traits from the Jahiliyyah—remained in Islam and were approved by it.

Title: Did Islam Spread by the Sword?
Full Content:
Question:

For further benefit, what is your view on the statement of those who say that Islam was spread by the sword, and we would like a logical response to them?

Answer:

This statement, in an absolute and unqualified sense, is false. Islam was spread through the call (Da’wah) to Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, and it was supported by the sword.

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, propagated it through preaching in Makkah for thirteen years, and then in Madinah before he was commanded to fight. The Companions and Muslims spread throughout the earth and called people to Allah, and whoever refused, they fought him in jihad, because the sword is an enforcement tool. Allah Almighty said: “…And We brought forth iron wherein is mighty power (in matters of war), as well as many benefits for mankind…“ [Al-Hadid: 25], and He said: “And fight them until there is no more Fitnah (disbelief and polytheism: i.e. worshipping others besides Allah) and the religion (worship) will all be for Allah Alone [in the whole of the world].” [Al-Anfal: 39].

“…And We brought forth iron wherein is mighty power (in matters of war), as well as many benefits for mankind…“

“And fight them until there is no more Fitnah (disbelief and polytheism: i.e. worshipping others besides Allah) and the religion (worship) will all be for Allah Alone [in the whole of the world].”

Whoever refused, they fought him for his own benefit and salvation—just as someone who owes a right to another human being must be compelled to fulfill that right, even through imprisonment or beating, and is not considered wronged. So how can anyone denounce or find it strange to compel someone who owes a right to Allah to fulfill His right? And how much more so when it is the greatest and most obligatory of rights, which is the Tawhid (Oneness) of Allah, the Glorified, and abandoning the association of partners with Him?

Out of Allah the Almighty’s mercy, He legislated jihad against the polytheists and fighting them until they worship Allah alone and abandon the worship of anything besides Him. In that lies their happiness and salvation in this world and the Hereafter, and Allah is the Grantor of success.

Title: The Ruling on Breeding and Selling Wild Animals
Full Content:

Answer:
